accuracy.evidence: Every beat count was checked word by word against spoken syllables (cat 1, rab-bit 2, but-ter-fly 3, strong 1, ba-na-na 3, el-e-phant 3, com-pu-ter 3, cat-er-pil-lar 4, pump-kin 2, ti-ger 2, to-ma-to 3, kite 1, cake 1, train 1) and every letter count quoted in feedback (strong 6, banana 6, butterfly 9, caterpillar 11, elephant 8) was counted. The written splits rab|bit, car|rot, thun|der and to|ma|to are uncontested and the first three are the national curriculum's own Year 1 examples; banana was kept out of the chop step because dictionary hyphenation (ba·nan·a) differs from its spoken beats.

misconceptions.evidence: Targets the three documented slips in early syllable work: counting letters instead of beats (Letters are not beats step with strong vs banana, challenge tag 'letters', m2, m6, m8), counting every vowel letter including a silent final e (cake prediction, SORT_TIP for cake, challenge tag 'vowels' on kite, m3) and blurring or dropping a beat when rushing (challenge tag 'short', 'Say it slowly' feedback on too few claps). Blending in the wrong order (bowrain, cornpop) is caught in the glue step and p3/m4.

lab_distinct.evidence: The lab is built on the beat structure of words: a clap counter judged against the word's parts with the parts lighting up per clap, a letters-versus-beats comparison card, ordered syllable gluing into rainbow/popcorn/dinosaur, a letter row where you tap gaps to cut a written word and check the pieces, and a beats sorter. No other flagship cuts written words or counts claps, and gate_lab_distinct passes under 30% against every flag lab including flagaloud and flagwread.

lab_teaches.evidence: The child does it first and the lab answers: two claps for cat get 'Too many claps. Say cat in one go', strong then banana end on a card showing 6 letters / 1 beat beside 6 letters / 3 beats, the wrong glue order gets 'bowrain is not a word', a cut at r|abbit gets 'right number of pieces! Now say each piece', and only then do the step texts name the rule (count claps not letters, each piece has one vowel sound).

predictions.evidence: Four predictions, each with a tempting wrong option the lab then disproves: butterfly 2 or 3 claps (children often hear butter + fly), strong and banana the same beats because both have 6 letters, rabbit split as ra | bbit (keeping the double b together), and cake as 2 beats because it has two vowel letters. Each is answered by the step's own clapping, cutting or sorting.

challenge_feedback.evidence: Six challenge words with two wrong options each, every wrong option tagged with its slip and given its own message: 'That is the number of letters. Clap dog: claps, not letters', 'kite has two vowel letters, but the e at the end is quiet. One beat', 'A beat got missed. Say it slowly: to-ma-to', and 'One clap too many' for over-counting. The smoke run on iPhone 13 showed each message for the matching tag.

readability.evidence: Kid text scores FK grade -1.4 (family target 5.0) with sentences such as 'Say cat. Clap one time.'; the adult text scores 8.3 (target 10). Lab copy uses only short instructions ('Tap Clap, then Done', 'Tap between two letters to cut it'), and the young class gives 56 px buttons with larger text.

no_filler.evidence: No filler phrases (gate_content passes). Each kid paragraph introduces one idea (beats, the word syllable, long words with one beat, gluing and cutting), and the adult paragraphs cover why it matters for reading and spelling, what the lab does, the three common mistakes with the chin trick, and a home activity, with no repeated template text from sibling lessons.

mobile.evidence: Checked on 360 px Android and iPhone 13 screenshots of all six steps: the clap pad and Done button fill the lower canvas, the six letter tiles of rabbit fit across at about 50 px each with the Check button below, the three beat bins sit side by side with clap icons and labels readable, and every action is repeated as a big button under the canvas.

accessibility.evidence: Everything works from buttons as well as taps and drags: Clap/Done, one button per glue part, one button per cut position (aria-label 'Cut after rab', marked with scissors when cut) plus Check, and one button per beat bin. The canvas aria-label is rewritten after every action (e.g. 'Yes! rab-bit: 2 claps. Word: butterfly. Claps so far: 0.') and axe WCAG 2.1 AA is clean in both themes on desktop and phone.
